                    ### Question
                    A 69-year-old man undergoes modified radical neck dissection for an oropharyngeal tumor. During the procedure, he requires multiple blood transfusions. Four hours after the surgery, examination shows that the right and left pupils do not constrict when a light is shone into the left eye. When light is shone into the right eye, both pupils constrict. Fundoscopic examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely location of the lesion?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Optic nerve
opb. Pretectal nuclei
opc. Superior cervical ganglion
opd. Edinger-Westphal nucleus
ope. Ciliary ganglion

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The most likely location of the lesion causing the pupil abnormalities is the Edinger-Westphal nucleus, as the efferent pathway controlling the left pupil is affected. This conclusion is supported by the fact that the right and left pupils do not constrict when light is shone into the left eye, indicating an afferent defect in the left eye with the efferent pathway intact.
